deck.name: Cell Biology Starter
deck.subject: Biology
deck.description: A sample deck that shows every question format. Delete it any time.

cards.q: Which organelle is the site of aerobic respiration?
cards.cloze: Aerobic respiration takes place in the {{mitochondria|mitochondrion}}.
false: Aerobic respiration takes place in the ribosomes.
cards.explain: Mitochondria run the Krebs cycle and oxidative phosphorylation, which produce most of the cell's ATP.

cards.q: Which organelle modifies and packages proteins for secretion?
cards.cloze: Proteins are modified and packaged into vesicles by the {{Golgi apparatus|Golgi}}.
false: The lysosome packages proteins into secretory vesicles.
cards.explain: Proteins made on the rough ER travel in vesicles to the Golgi, which adds carbohydrates and sorts them.

cards.q: What is the site of protein synthesis in a cell?
false: Proteins are synthesised inside the nucleus.
cards.explain: mRNA is translated at ribosomes, either free in the cytoplasm or attached to the rough ER.

cards.cloze: {{Lysosomes|Lysosome}} contain hydrolytic enzymes that break down worn out organelles.
cards.explain: Lysosomes are vesicles of hydrolytic enzymes used to digest pathogens and old organelles (autolysis).

cards.q: What is the function of the nucleolus?
cards.cloze: The nucleolus is where {{ribosomes}} are made.
false: The nucleolus stores the cell's DNA.
cards.explain: The nucleolus makes ribosomal RNA and assembles ribosome subunits.

cards.q: What size are the ribosomes in prokaryotic cells?
false: Prokaryotic cells have 80S ribosomes, the same as eukaryotes.
cards.explain: Prokaryotes have 70S ribosomes, eukaryotes have larger 80S ribosomes in their cytoplasm.

cards.q: What are small circular loops of DNA in bacteria called?
cards.cloze: Many bacteria carry extra genes, such as antibiotic resistance, on {{plasmids|plasmid}}.
false: Plasmids are found in the nucleus of eukaryotic cells.
cards.explain: Plasmids replicate independently and can be passed between bacteria, spreading resistance genes.

cards.q: What is the bacterial cell wall made of?
cards.cloze: Bacterial cell walls are made of {{murein|peptidoglycan}}.
false: Bacterial cell walls are made of cellulose.
cards.explain: Murein (peptidoglycan) is a glycoprotein. Plant cell walls are cellulose, fungal walls are chitin.

cards.q: What is the formula for magnification?
false: Magnification equals actual size divided by image size.
cards.explain: Magnification = image size ÷ actual size. Rearrange to $A = \frac{I}{M}$ to find the real size of a specimen.

cards.q: An image is 50 mm long at ×1000 magnification. What is the actual length in µm?
cards.cloze: A 50 mm image at ×1000 is {{50 µm|50}} long in real life.
cards.explain: $A = \frac{I}{M} = \frac{50\,000\ \mu m}{1000} = 50\ \mu m$. Convert to the same units first.

cards.q: Which type of microscope gives a 3D image of a specimen's surface?
cards.cloze: A {{scanning electron microscope|SEM}} produces 3D images of surfaces.
false: A transmission electron microscope produces 3D images of surfaces.
cards.explain: SEMs bounce electrons off the surface. TEMs pass electrons through thin sections and give higher resolution 2D images.

cards.q: Why do electron microscopes have a higher resolution than light microscopes?
answers: electrons have shorter wavelength than light
cards.cloze: Electron microscopes resolve more detail because electrons have a {{shorter wavelength}} than light.
false: Electron microscopes have higher resolution because they magnify more.
cards.explain: Resolution is limited by wavelength. A shorter wavelength lets two close points be seen as separate.

cards.q: What is the name of the model describing membrane structure?
cards.cloze: Membrane structure is described by the {{fluid mosaic}} model.
false: Membrane structure is described by the induced fit model.
cards.explain: Fluid because phospholipids move freely; mosaic because proteins are scattered through the bilayer.

cards.q: Which molecule regulates membrane fluidity in animal cells?
cards.cloze: {{Cholesterol}} sits between phospholipids and makes the membrane less fluid.
false: Glycoproteins regulate the fluidity of the membrane.
cards.explain: Cholesterol binds phospholipid tails, pulling them together and reducing fluidity and permeability.

cards.q: Put the stages of mitosis in order
cards.explain: Chromosomes condense (P), line up on the equator (M), sister chromatids are pulled apart (A), then two nuclei form (T).

cards.q: Order the journey of a secreted protein
steps: Made on ribosomes on the rough ER
Transported in a vesicle to the Golgi
Modified and packaged by the Golgi
Vesicle fuses with the cell membrane (exocytosis)
cards.explain: This pathway links several organelles and is a favourite six-mark question.

cards.q: Compare the structure of prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells.
points: Prokaryotes have no nucleus; DNA is free in the cytoplasm
Prokaryotic DNA is circular and not associated with histones
Prokaryotic cell walls are made of murein
Prokaryotes may have plasmids, a capsule and flagella
cards.explain: Aim for paired comparisons: say what each type has, not just what one lacks.
